name: Homewood
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Homewood, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Homewood, IL: Holiday Lights with Santa on a fire engine, a holiday train on Ridge Road, Skate with Santa and a lighted trail walk.
lede: Homewood saves its biggest Christmas night for Holiday Lights, when downtown fills with carolers, a carousel and a holiday train, and Santa arrives on a Homewood fire engine to light the tree at Irwin Park.
celebrates: The Village of Homewood and the Homewood-Flossmoor Park District sponsor Holiday Lights each December around Martin Avenue and Ridge Road downtown. Carolers stroll the streets, Elsa, Rapunzel and Holiday Belle sing and dance, children ride a holiday carousel and a trackless train, and ice carvers work in Martin Square. A parade with Santa steps off from the fire station, and Santa counts down to the tree lighting at Irwin Park, then visits with kids while they make reindeer food. The Homewood Science Center shows holiday films, and a Holiday Market follows on Saturday. The park district adds Letters from Santa, Skate with Santa and a lighted trail walk at Irons Oaks.
lastyear: In 2025 Holiday Lights was planned for Friday, December 5, from 5 to 9 p.m. in historic downtown Homewood. The village's plan included Elsa, Rapunzel and Holiday Belle, carousel and train rides at Ridge Road and Martin Avenue, free mini cakes from Little Spruce Microbakery, 1,000 collectible mugs and cookie decorating. A Santa parade was set to leave the fire department at 6:50 p.m. before the 7 p.m. tree lighting at Irwin Park. The HF Chronicle later ran a photo of the holiday train circling Ridge Road during the 2025 festival.
facts: Homewood was founded in 1893, and its historic downtown grew up where Dixie Highway meets Ridge Road. Ridge Road follows the Calumet Shoreline, an ancient shoreline that still shows as a sand ridge through town. The Homewood-Flossmoor Park District, which lights the tree at Irwin Park, was founded in 1969 and unveiled a brand new logo in 2026. Holiday Lights sells a limited run of 1,000 commemorative mugs, and the park district's Light Up Trail Walk at Irons Oaks reaches its fourth year in 2026.
trains: Homewood is a train town. Its station is a former Illinois Central Railroad depot built in 1923 and shared by Metra Electric and Amtrak, whose Illini, Saluki and City of New Orleans trains stop here, with Kankakee the next Amtrak stop south. A tunnel from 1911 runs under the tracks to link downtown with the west side. In 2007 the village opened a railfan viewing platform beside the Canadian National main line, where train counts often top 100 a day, with an Illinois Central locomotive and caboose on display. At Holiday Lights, a trackless holiday train circles Ridge Road.

faq: What is Holiday Lights in Homewood?

Holiday Lights is Homewood's main Christmas celebration, sponsored by the Village of Homewood and the Homewood-Flossmoor Park District. Downtown around Martin Avenue and Ridge Road fills with carolers, live music, ice carving, a holiday carousel and a trackless train for one evening, and Santa arrives on a fire engine to light the tree at Irwin Park.
Where is the Homewood Christmas tree lit?

At Irwin Park, which the park district lists at 18120 Highland Avenue. Families gather as Santa arrives aboard a Homewood fire engine, and Santa leads a countdown before the tree lights up with thousands of lights. Afterward, children can meet Santa, share their wish lists and make reindeer food.
Where can kids see Santa in Homewood?

Santa rides in the Holiday Lights parade, lights the tree at Irwin Park and then visits with children. The Homewood-Flossmoor Park District also hosts Skate with Santa at the H-F Ice Arena and runs Santa Driveway Visits for H-F residents, and children can mail Santa a letter at the Irwin Community Center and get one back.
Is there a train at Homewood's Christmas celebration?

Yes. Holiday Lights brings a trackless holiday train, which the HF Chronicle calls the Holiday Express, that circles Ridge Road next to the holiday carousel. Homewood also has a real train station on the Metra Electric Line and a railfan viewing platform beside the busy Canadian National main line, a short walk from downtown shops.
Who runs Christmas events in Homewood?

The Village of Homewood runs Holiday Lights and the Holiday Market, led by its Community Events Manager. The Homewood-Flossmoor Park District, which serves both Homewood and Flossmoor, handles the tree lighting at Irwin Park, Letters from Santa, Skate with Santa at the H-F Ice Arena and the Light Up Trail Walk at Irons Oaks.
